title: Sperner's Lemma via Door-Counting Parity (Abstract CellComplex)
description: Proves Sperner's lemma for finite cell families with adjacency axioms using door-counting parity. Key results: even cardinality of fixed-point-free involutions (useful for Tucker's lemma/Borsuk-Ulam), door-count parity equals surjectivity, exists_panchromatic when boundary doors are odd. 17 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

overview.historicalContext: Sperner's lemma (1928): in any Sperner-labeled triangulation, the number of fully-labeled simplices is odd. The door-counting proof is purely combinatorial and works for abstract cell families satisfying adjacency axioms, without geometric structure.
overview.problemStatement: Prove Sperner's lemma via door-counting for abstract finite cell families with face-sharing adjacency axioms.
overview.proofStrategy: Define 'doors' as edges colored with all d+1 colors. Interior doors pair via the adjacency involution (even count). Per-cell: #door positions is odd iff coloring is surjective. Sum: panchromatic count ≡ boundary door count (mod 2). If boundary has odd doors, a panchromatic cell exists.
keyInsights: **Abstract adjacency interface**: each cell has d+1 faces indexed by Fin(d+1). adj s k returns Some(s',k') or none — enough structure for the parity proof.
**Involution parity lemma**: even_card_fpf_invol is useful beyond Sperner (Tucker's lemma, Borsuk-Ulam).
**Boundary door count**: with a Sperner coloring, every boundary door lies on the last face (boundary_doors_on_last_face).

sections.title: Abstract Door-Counting Sperner Proof
sections.mathContext: Panchromatic count $\equiv$ boundary door count $\pmod{2}$; odd boundary $\Rightarrow$ $\exists$ panchromatic cell.

conclusion.summary: 17 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms. Abstract Sperner's lemma proved for any cell family satisfying door-counting axioms.
conclusion.implications: This abstract formulation makes Sperner's lemma applicable to any finite combinatorial structure satisfying the adjacency axioms, enabling diverse topological applications.
openQuestions: Can Tucker's lemma be proved from this abstract framework?
Can the Z/2-index theorem be derived from even_card_fpf_invol?
Can the Borsuk-Ulam theorem be proved via this abstract door-counting?
